key_terms.الشَّدِيدُ: The severe/harsh one (referring to the person subject to hadd)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for stealing from public treasury versus private property in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) articulates a nuanced jurisprudential distinction in the Bayt al-Mal, ruling that stealing from public funds incurs no fixed hadd (corporal punishment) because it is viewed as 'Allah's property consuming Allah's property,' provided the thief returns the equivalent value. This contrasts with private theft, where the standard hadd of hand amputation applies, reflecting the unique status of public treasury assets in Shia legal theory. This ruling highlights the flexibility of hadd punishments when the victim is the collective Muslim community rather than an individual.
